status: proposed 2026-10-05; changes published scores, so it waits for Max's ruling (cos decision). decided_on is the draft date; a release sets it to the ruling's date. proposed_regenerations.json and proposed_exclusions.json are alternatives: a release adopts one of them, not both.
basis: policybench/reference_exclusions.py: an output is excluded for every model when its reference depends on an engine input the prompt never listed and a careful reader could take the stated facts the other way.

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes. Minnesota Paid Leave premiums "accrue and become payable by each employer" (Minn. Stat. 268B.14, subd. 1); the employer must pay at least 50 percent, and employees pay through wage deductions only "the remaining portion, if any, of the premium not paid by the employer" (subd. 3), so the employee share runs from 0 to 0.44% of wages at the employer's choice. The reference counts the largest employee share the employer may deduct (mn_employee_paid_leave_contribution $127.60), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as an employer premium that is not a mandatory employee tax, or with an employer that does not deduct it, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone, the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).
exclusions.unlisted_input: whether the employer deducts the employee share of Minnesota Paid Leave from wages, which the law permits but does not require (Minn. Stat. 268B.14, subds. 1, 3 and 5a)
exclusions.note: Found 2026-10-05 by classifying every state program in the payroll references from primary law (reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll/program_classification.json) and sweeping all 1,984 outputs with the programs classified as optional employer pass-through left out of employee state payroll tax; that moves this output alone in its household and no other output. The frozen value has been the reference since the first run (2026-06-15).

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes. Colorado FAMLI premiums are remitted by the employer (C.R.S. 8-13.3-507(2)), which "may deduct up to 50 percent of the premium" from wages (507(5)); an employer that deducts less is considered to have elected to pay the rest (7 CCR 1107-1 s. 1.4(6)(A)). The reference counts the largest employee share the employer may deduct (co_employee_famli_contribution $17.99), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as an employer premium that is not a mandatory employee tax, or with an employer that does not deduct it, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone, the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).
exclusions.unlisted_input: whether the employer deducts the employee share of Colorado FAMLI from wages, which the law permits but does not require (C.R.S. 8-13.3-507(2), (3)(b) and (5); 7 CCR 1107-1 s. 1.4(6)(A))
exclusions.note: Found 2026-10-05 by classifying every state program in the payroll references from primary law (reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll/program_classification.json) and sweeping all 1,984 outputs with the programs classified as optional employer pass-through left out of employee state payroll tax; that moves this output alone in its household and no other output. The frozen value has been the reference since the first run (2026-06-15).

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes. Massachusetts PFML contributions are remitted by the employer (M.G.L. c. 175M, s. 6(a)), which may deduct up to 100 percent of the family and 40 percent of the medical contribution from wages (s. 6(c)) and may choose to deduct less (458 CMR 2.05(5)(c)). The reference counts the largest employee share the employer may deduct (ma_employee_paid_leave_contribution $805.01), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as an employer premium that is not a mandatory employee tax, or with an employer that does not deduct it, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone, the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).

exclusions.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes. New York's covered employer must provide disability and Paid Family Leave coverage and pays its cost beyond what it collects (N.Y. Workers' Compensation Law s. 210(1)); the employer "is authorized to collect" employee contributions up to the statutory caps by payroll deduction (s. 209(4)), and the Workers' Compensation Board says an employer "is allowed, but not required" to collect them. The reference counts the largest employee share the employer may deduct (ny_employee_disability_benefits_contribution $31.20, ny_employee_paid_family_leave_contribution $411.91), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as an employer premium that is not a mandatory employee tax, or with an employer that does not deduct it, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone, the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).
exclusions.unlisted_input: whether the employer deducts the employee share of New York Paid Family Leave and Disability Benefits from wages, which the law permits but does not require (N.Y. Workers' Compensation Law ss. 209(3)-(4) and 210(1))
